title: Duchy of Oldenburg
capsule: The Duchy of Oldenburg was a north German principality on the lower Weser coast, a possession of the House of Oldenburg (also the ruling dynasty of Denmark) that was raised briefly to duchy status before Napoleon annexed it outright in December 1810, citing its duke Peter Friedrich Ludwig's refusal to enforce the Continental System. At the Congress of Vienna (1815), the restored duchy was elevated to the Grand Duchy of Oldenburg and compensated with the Principality of Birkenfeld, though its original territory had been occupied by France for five years. Grand Duke Paul Friedrich August (r. 1829–1853) oversaw modest liberal reforms; the grand duchy joined the North German Confederation in 1867 and was absorbed into the German Empire in 1871. Oldenburg's dynastic house had supplied several European monarchs, including the kings of Denmark, Sweden, and Greece.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The duchy's territorial limits are well-documented in Napoleonic-era and Congress of Vienna sources; the 1806–1871 period is unambiguous administratively.
